findings.where: First screen, the hero photograph, desktop and phone. On desktop it is the giant keyed-out head on the right. On phone it is the floating head, cut off at the neck, between the nav and the heading.
findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of Mark speaking, with his line over it. Here the backdrop is keyed away to flat slate and the face is blown up far beyond life size. What is left is a cut-out head on a dark field, with no lectern, audience or event to show he is speaking somewhere. When you squint, the face outweighs the heading and becomes the first thing you see. The first screen reads as a dark-ground portrait tile (v4 or v6), not v7. The huge close-up face feels like a campaign poster rather than a quiet advisor's page.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and needs this tile to stand for the 'Mark at work' direction it was built for. Development-bank staff (the audience) would also object, because an oversized face crowding the page reads as self-promotion rather than the refined, reserved standing the brief asks for.

findings.where: First screen, the placeholder caption at the bottom left ('Placeholder: Mark's photo from the current site…'), desktop
findings.fault: The caption belongs to the photograph on the right, but it sits under the text column at the far left, about 400 px from the image. By proximity it reads as a footnote to Mark's line and the email action, not as a label on the photo.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile, who has to work out which element the placeholder note refers to. A visitor might also read 'Placeholder' as applying to the words or the contact.
